non_blocking_issues: The int128 range of a_eval is narrower than it looks, but it can only affect keep decisions. A Hadamard bound on the Bareiss products (bounds.py) shows the current 14 SAMPLES cannot overflow at n<=8 (worst case: 7.4e35 against 1.7e38 at n=8; 2.5e30 at n=7). It does not extend to general q=64 samples: at q=64 the safe range is p<=590 (beta<=9.2) for n=7 and p<=191 (beta<=2.98) for n=8. Outside that range overflow actually happens: my tests found wrong values at n=7 with p in {1866, 2090, 2746, 2991} and at n=8 with p as low as 944. The P/U flag only ever leads to keeping a graph (P is kept, U goes to the exact resolver), so overflow there cannot drop anything. Still, anyone adding samples later should recheck bounds.py. Signed int128 overflow is undefined behaviour and nothing detects it at runtime; adding __builtin_mul_overflow or -ftrapv would cost almost nothing.

The Descartes path that drops graphs is safe with a large margin. At n=7 every intermediate is at most 1.7e18 (Bareiss at beta<=10 about 9.4e16, m!*coef about 2.8e14, Horner check at u=m+1 about 1.7e18); at n=8 at most 8.8e21. These are about 1.5e-8 of the 2^127 limit at n=7 and 4.4e-3 at n=8 when the sample path is included.

fastregion._replay_isolation does not fully certify sympy's root isolation. It checks the per-polynomial root counts (Sturm) and that each interval's factor f changes sign across it. It does not check that f divides the attributed polynomial, or that each interval holds exactly one root of the union of all the polynomials. So if sympy put a root of a0 and a different root of a1 into one interval, the replay would still pass and the cell between those two roots would never be sampled. This is a theoretical gap that depends on trusting sympy. For this dataset it is closed by my independent full recomputation (below), which agrees exactly.

resolve_U.py (lines 52-54) drops a line whose verdict is neither 'positivity_possible' nor 'never'; the fail-safe choice is to keep it. With positivity_only=True, region() can only return those two verdicts or raise, and the stats files show other_verdict=0 in all four parts, so nothing was lost here. Keeping those lines would make the code safe against future changes to region().

One-line justification for the region() drop: by Lemma A.2 the a_i are t-free, the legal set is t>0 with beta>2+1/t, and the union of those beta ranges over all legal t is exactly (2, inf). {beta>2 : all a_i>0} is open and its boundary lies in the roots of the a_i. So one sample in each gap between isolating intervals, plus beta_min+... and last+1, decides it exactly. Roots at exactly 2 are excluded, and so are roots below 2: I checked that inf=2 with strict=True returns 2 as a degenerate interval, which is filtered out, and returns nothing below 2.
A note for the runbook, not a soundness issue: geng res/mod classes at n=7 are very uneven. 17/300 is empty, while 5/40 holds about 2e8 digraphs after directg.
checks_performed: (1) N convention. filter7p sets N[i][j] = (i!=j && A[j][i]==0). This is the same as fastregion.nonedge_matrix (1 - A[sigma_j][sigma_i]) and matches CLAUDE.md section 2: W[i][j] is weak iff A[j][i]=1. I proved it from Lemma A(i) and also checked it end to end. On 1,400 random legal (eps, delta) points over real N- and U-dropped 7-node graphs, the x from ctln.analyze_support equals c*a(beta) exactly, with a computed by sympy (x_i a_j = x_j a_i for all i, j and one common scale). The scale c was positive 1,580 times and negative 820 times; a negative scale means D<0, which by A.2 rules out stability.

(2) a_eval. (qI+pN)[i<-q1] = q*(I+(p/q)N)[i<-1], so the determinant is q^n a_i(p/q). With q>0 the sign is preserved. Checked exactly against sympy DomainMatrix over ZZ[beta] for 6,000 random graphs (5,400 with 7 nodes, 600 with 8; densities 0.05 to 1.0). That is 979,800 evaluations covering the 14 filter samples, 6 random q=64 points inside the proven-safe range, 2 points with q=1 and beta up to 50, and 1 point with beta<2: 0 mismatches.

(3) descartes_nonpositive. The forward-difference recurrence, the falling-factorial recurrence FF_k = FF_{k-1}*(u-(k-1)) updated in place from high j to low, and the exact m!/k! scaling all check out. The u=m+1 test is a valid degree check: a_i has degree <=m-1 and m+1 nodes are used. The C coefficients equal m! times the coefficients of a_i(2+u) from sympy for all 6,000 graphs × n values of i. The drop rule is sound: if every coefficient of a_i(2+u) is <=0, then a_i(beta)<=0 for every beta>2, and that covers a_i identically 0. Lemma A.2 says a stable fixed point forces D>0 and x=(theta/eps)a/D, so x>0 requires every a_i>0 strictly. Legal parameters always have beta>2+1/t>2. As a further check, 3,000 real N-dropped graphs (from a 1,000,000-digraph geng/directg slice) were each re-certified with sympy: some a_i(2+u) has all coefficients <=0.

(4) Overflow. bounds.py gives rigorous Hadamard bounds for every int128 intermediate: Bareiss products of (c+1)-minors, forward differences, m!*coefficients, and Horner at (m+1)^m. The Descartes and sample paths are all safe for n<=8. It also computes the q=64 safe ranges, and the overflows I observed outside them match the bound.

(5) Domination. The C test is k dominates j iff A[j][k]=1, A[k][j]=0, and no i outside {j,k} has A[i][j]=1 and A[i][k]=0. This matches Lemma D, graphs.graphically_dominates, and the text of Curto 2510.05098 Def. 1.1, which I read in the scratchpad PDF. The paper uses W_ij = -1+eps when j->i, the same edge direction as ours. I re-derived Lemma D's proof term by term; it needs only eps>0, delta>=0 and uniform theta. My Python domination test agrees with C on 6,000 random graphs. On 800 random legal points over dominated graphs, ctln never gave x>0.

(6) resolve_U and region(..., INF, positivity_only=True). For full support the polynomials are exactly the a_i (the o_k dict is empty). An identically zero a_i gives 'never'. The test is strict a_i(sample)>0 with one sample per cell on (2, inf), and the replay runs before the result is returned. Independent recomputation of all 786,596 n=7 U lines: I used the C harness coefficients (validated against sympy above) and my own exact decider, which builds a coprime squarefree base with Fraction Euclid, isolates roots by Descartes bisection, refines until roots of different factors are separated, and samples every gap. It does not use sympy or fastregion. Result: 63,586 POS and 723,010 NEVER. Both sets are identical to the resolver's (R lines and droppedU files), with 0 disagreements and 0 errors. Every U line is domination-free and not N-dropped. The same decider on the 427 n=6 U lines gives 38 positive, matching the resolver set exactly.

End-to-end check with ctln.analyze_support, the project's verifier using the CLAUDE.md W: 3,600 random legal points over 700 N-dropped, 700 U-dropped and 400 dominated real 7-node graphs, two points each, with eps from 1/2 to 1/200 and q pushed close to 1. No point gave a positive full-support fixed point whose stability was True or undecided.

Relabelling invariance: 105,000 graphs (100,000 from the real slice plus 5,000 U-dropped), each run through the unmodified filter7p copy and under a random vertex permutation. The P/U/drop decision changed for 0 of them.

Known counterexamples survive. All 123 n=7 limit counterexamples are kept (121 P and 2 U); both U ones resolve as positive in fastregion and in my independent decider (at beta 4429/2048 and 16999/8192). &FNFL~[udo? and Geneson's graph are kept as P.

With positivity_only=True, region() can only return those two verdicts (any exception crashes the run instead), and all four n=7 stats files show other_verdict = 0. All 722,010 dropped-U lines carry the reason 'no legal beta with all a_i > 0'. Still, the safe default is to keep anything not proven 'never'.

filter7p.c has no runtime overflow guard in det128/a_eval. Safety rests on |matrix entries| <= max(p,q) <= 129 (from the sample 1/64, i.e. p=129, q=64) and n <= 8. The Hadamard argument puts every Bareiss intermediate below 2^118.8 at n=8 (descartes path below 2^105.4). The safe entry bound from that argument is 193 at n=8 and 591 at n=7. A probe with entries of 3200 (beta=50 written over q=64) overflowed silently, as expected. A future edit to SAMPLES with max(p,q) > 193 at n=8 would corrupt results without any error. Suggest a static assert or __builtin_mul_overflow checks.

resolve_U.py uses 'assert f == "U"' to check the flag. Under python -O this is stripped and an unexpected flag would be resolved instead of rejected. That is harmless: it only causes extra analysis, never a drop.

Scope: every drop (domination via Lemma D / Corollary D.3, and positivity via Lemma A.2) is justified for FULL support only. The survivor set must not be reused to skip graphs when analysing smaller supports: a dominated 7-node graph can still have a stable fixed point on a smaller support, and condition 2 (the off-support condition, o_k < 0) is not part of this filter.

U-resolution soundness also depends on sympy 1.14's VAS isolation and factorization. The replay (Sturm count per polynomial plus a sign change in each interval) checks counts but does not check that each irreducible factor actually divides the polynomial it is attributed to. My independent Sturm-bisection ground truth agreed on every case tested, but those tests are samples, not a proof for all 722,010 n=7 U-drops.

In REPRODUCE_n7_finite.md the 'geng | directg | filter7p' pipelines run without pipefail. A truncated upstream would only be caught by the required total-count check (882,033,440). That check is present and passes.

C: N[i][j] = (i!=j && A[j][i]==0). fastregion.nonedge_matrix: 1 - A[sigma_j][sigma_i]. Both are the same receiver-first nonedge matrix. Curto 2510.05098 eq. (1.3) uses the same edge convention (W_ij = -1+eps if j->i); I read it from the PDF text.

(1') N convention, end to end. For every tested graph I built I - W in exact rationals from CLAUDE.md W at a random eps = k/64 with beta = p/64, solved (I - W) x = 1, and checked that x is exactly proportional to the harness's a_eval vector. This has no N matrix in the loop. 0 failures.

(2) a_eval. The scaling argument: q*C[i<-1] = (qI + pN)[i<-q1], so the determinant is q^m a_i(p/q), sign preserved for q>0. Tested by exact integer equality of the C a_eval against 64^m * a_i(p/64), with a_i from sympy Berkowitz on the symbolic C[i<-1], at p in {129,130,131,133,136,144,160,176,192}. 0 mismatches.

(3) descartes_nonpositive. I re-derived the steps: forward differences, Newton form p(u) = sum D_k * C(u,k), m!/k! scaling, the in-place falling-factorial recurrence (descending j), and the Horner check at u = m+1. The C coefficients equal the sympy expansion of m!*a_i(2+u) exactly for every i of every tested graph. The drop logic: all coefficients <= 0 gives a_i(2+u) <= 0 for u>0, i.e. for every beta > 2. Lemma A.2 (a stable K has det K > 0, and adj(K)1 = adj(C)1 does not depend on t) requires strict a_i > 0 at some single beta > 2. So the drop is valid at every legal (eps, delta), and also when a_i is identically 0.

(6') Legal range. eps in (0,1) and delta > 0 map bijectively to t > 0 and beta > 1. Legality q > 1 is equivalent to beta > 2 + 1/t, and the union over t > 0 is exactly the open ray beta > 2. Both the C path (u > 0) and region() (b_min = 2, roots at 2 removed, open cells) use that open ray.

(4) __int128 overflow. Hadamard bounds for products of two (k-1)-order Bareiss minors: n=8 with entries <= 129 gives 2^118.8; with beta = 50, q = 1 gives 2^99.7; descartes evaluations (entries <= 11) give 2^69.1. Forward differences <= 2^47.7, scale <= 2^63.0, coefficients <= 2^79.8 (unsigned Stirling numbers of the first kind <= 13132), Horner at u = m+1 <= 2^105.4. All are below 2^127. The largest intermediate measured by a bigint replica of det128/descartes over all tested graphs is 2^100 (n=8) and 2^87 (n=7).

(5) Domination. Curto 2510.05098 Definition 1.1 extracted verbatim from the arXiv PDF matches filter7p.domination_free and graphs.graphically_dominates exactly: (ii) j->k and k-/->j; (i) every i->j has i->k. I also proved the full-support prune myself without the paper: from y_k - y_j >= -(1-eps)x_j + (1+delta)x_k and x = y on the support it follows that 0 >= eps*x_j + delta*x_k, a contradiction for every eps>0, delta>=0. This uses both halves of (ii). Empirically, no dominated graph in any test set (1,089 in total) had all a_i > 0 at any beta > 2.

(6) resolve_U / region(positivity_only=True). For full support o is empty, so Stage 1 decides exactly whether some open cell of (2, inf) between the isolated roots of all a_i has every a_i > 0 at its sample. Because {beta : all a_i > 0} is open, that is exactly 'exists beta > 2 with all a_i > 0'. I checked sympy 1.14's strict=True disjoining (strict separation), the removal of roots exactly at b_min, and the refinement of the first interval.

Independent ground truth. I wrote my own Fraction Sturm-sequence cell decomposition, with no sympy root isolation: squarefree lcm of the a_i, (beta-2) factors removed, Cauchy bound, bisection until each piece holds at most one root, and a proof that the sample set hits every cell. It passed 11 synthetic unit tests, including windows of width 1e-6. Its decision was compared with every drop and every 'P' flag in all test sets, and with region() on every U line.

non_blocking_issues: A witness at a fixed eta = 10^-6 is not guaranteed to exist. Openness only promises some eta > 0. The n=7 limit hit &F]VhW[rSp? has its stable curve cell at (1916, inf); at the sample t = 1917, beta = 2 + 1/t + 10^-6 is NOT stable (minor 6 negative), while 10^-7 down to 10^-12 are stable. n7/validate_curve_test.py and the note's section 3.2 witness procedure use a fixed 10^-6 and would raise a false 'witness failure' if applied at n=7. Fix: shrink eta until stable, which always terminates. This cannot make a 'never' verdict wrong.

fastregion._cells checks that isolating intervals are strictly separated with a Python `assert`, and curve_test checks P[0]==[1] with an `assert`. Under `python -O` both checks are silently skipped. sympy strict=True guarantees separation and the repo never uses -O, but for a certifying path `raise` would be safer than `assert`.

When some cell is stable, curve_test reports 'stable_somewhere' and the escalated cells of that graph are no longer counted in the verdict. This is conservative because such graphs go to region2d anyway, but the escalation count is lost. G3's claim of '0 escalations' should count escalated cells, not verdicts.

The edges >= 22 cut (B > Nn) is proved only for the FULL support at m = 7. For supports of size 5 or 6 inside n = 7, the valid necessary condition is B_sigma > Nn_sigma on the induced subgraph (same proof applied to K_sigma). The whole-graph edge column of n7_pos_all_PU.txt.gz must not be used to prune those supports.

Section 3.2 of the note names notes/prover_scripts_M/curve1d.py as the implementation; production uses n7/curve_test.py. A diff shows the logic is identical: the interpolation assert became a raise, and P can now be passed in. Notation drift only.

Section 3.3 case (c2) at an irrational algebraic beta_l is not implemented, as the note itself says; this is covered only because curve survivors go to region2d. The proof of the strip decomposition itself is correct (re-derived).
checks_performed: (a) Remark F re-derived and checked symbolically: K(l*beta, l*t) = (1-l)I + l*K(beta,t), so spec maps mu -> (1-l) + l*mu and Re > 0 is kept for l in (0,1]. The '=>' direction uses only this exact affine spectral identity plus a scalar IVT; the root is explicit: lambda* = (1 + sqrt(1 + beta/t))/beta. lambda* > 2/beta always, and lambda* < 1 iff t(beta-2) > 1 (checked symbolically). The curve point satisfies t'(beta'-2) = 1. beta' = 2 + 1/t' > 2 is automatic; legality is needed only for beta > 2, so that (2/beta, 1) is nonempty. '<=' uses only openness, i.e. continuity of eigenvalues, or equivalently strict positivity of finitely many polynomial Hurwitz minors. Conclusion: 'never' on the whole curve t in (0, inf) excludes stability at every real legal (eps, delta), so it excludes a full-support SFP. Nothing else is used.

(a) (R+) checked: beta' = lambda* beta < beta. The strip decomposition was re-derived: the stable set on ray tau is (0, beta_s(tau)) (downward closed by Remark F, and open); legal is beta > 1 + sqrt(1 + 1/tau); the case split gives (c1) or (c2), both directions.

(a) Lemma R '=>' instance: both certificate witnesses of the FNFL candidate (eps=1/49 and eps=1/36) were re-verified as stable_fixed_point with ctln.analyze_support. Their ray projections t' were bracketed by exact rational bisection (r < t' iff (r*beta/t - 1) < 0 or (r*beta/t - 1)^2 < 1 + beta/t). Both brackets lie inside curve_test's stable cell (6, inf).
(b) L(t) = t*K(2+1/t, t) checked symbolically; since t > 0, det(mu I + L) is Hurwitz iff K is positive stable.

(b) Degree bound deg c_k <= k+1 re-derived via (T2) on principal blocks, and confirmed on 3,000 random graphs. coeff_polys matched an independent sympy QQ charpoly at 9,000 non-integer rational t. On all 3,129 tested graphs coeff_polys equals the symbolic ZZ[t] Berkowitz charpoly, and fastregion.hurwitz_det_poly(P, m-1) equals the symbolic Delta_{m-1}.

(b) Critical-set sufficiency was re-derived from Lemma B(d) with t as the parameter. p is monic of fixed degree, so roots are continuous and none escape. A root on iR means c_m = 0 or, by (b3), Delta_{m-1} = 0. Critical points themselves are never stable. Independent re-derivation without Lemma B on 3,129 graphs: ALL Hurwitz minors Delta_1..Delta_6 and all c_k were taken symbolically over ZZ[t], and the full arrangement of their positive roots was decided by Routh-Hurwitz (21,805 fine cells). Results: verdicts identical on every graph (2,128 never, 1,001 stable_somewhere); 0 stability changes at a root not dividing c_m or Delta_{m-1}; 0 mismatches over 16,979 fine cells lying inside coarse curve_test cells.

(b) fastregion._cells: the first-interval refinement above 0 was exercised directly (sqrt2 in (0,2) -> (1,2)). sympy dup_isolate_real_roots_list with inf=0 and strict=True was confirmed to drop negative roots, return exact rational roots as degenerate intervals, and return disjoint intervals.

(b) Three-valued handling: hurwitz_stable returns False only on a negative coefficient or minor, which proves 'not Hurwitz'. None leads to 2 re-samples and then 'escalate', never 'never'. A c_k (k >= 1) or Delta that is identically zero gives 'never'. This is sound because it is an identity on the whole curve: by (b1) no curve point is strictly stable, and Lemma R transports only strict stability, so no undecided point is collapsed. Checked on 40 random 7-node tournaments: all hit the c_2 == 0 branch, and 200 legal points were all not stable.

(b) coeff_never fast path: each c_k has constant sign on each cell, because all non-constant c_k roots are isolated jointly and the sample avoids them. Constant c_k are evaluated at every sample (constant negative gives never; constant zero is caught earlier). Roots carry a zero coefficient. Hence 'no sample with all c_k > 0' implies no t > 0 is Hurwitz (b1). Agreement: 0 disagreements between curve_test and curve_test_fast on 3,000 random n=7 graphs, all 9,608 n=5 graphs and all 129 hits/specials; 1,852 of the 3,000 were decided by coeff_never, and the full test also says 'never' for every one.

(b) Random n=7 graphs: 3,000 (sparse/medium Bernoulli, dense Bernoulli, K7 minus 1..21 arcs) gave 2,128 never, 872 stable_somewhere, 0 escalate. All 872 stable cells have a legal witness with ctln.analyze_support stable == True at beta = 2 + 1/t + 10^-6.

(b) 300 'never' graphs (all 276 that needed the full test plus 24 dense coeff_never graphs; edges 22-40) x 20 random exact legal points (10 within 1e-9..1e-3 of the curve, 10 broad; t in [1e-2, 1e4]): 6,000 points, 0 stable == True, 0 None.

The section 2.4 graphs have bounded stable cells (9,10) and (10,11), as the note states; FNFL's curve cell is (6, inf).

(c) The three 2x2 principal minors (bidirected 1+2t; non-adjacent (1-beta)(1+beta+2t); one-way 1-t(beta-2), both orientations) were checked symbolically, and e_2 = t*Phi + B + O - Nn(beta^2-1) was checked. Chain: e_2 - (B-Nn)(1+2t) = -Nn(beta^2-2+2t(beta-2)) + O(1-t(beta-2)), which is <= 0 at every legal point (beta > 2 and t(beta-2) > 1). So e_2 > 0 (needed by (b1)) forces B > Nn, including when Nn = 0. At m = 7, edges = 2B+O = 21+B-Nn, so B > Nn iff edges >= 22; this was verified over all (B, Nn, O) with B+Nn+O = 21.

(c) Exact test on 2,000 random graphs at 3,500 random legal points: e_2 computed independently from ctln.weight_matrix (K = (I-W)/eps, both as (tr^2 - tr K^2)/2 and as a sum of 2x2 minors) equals both closed forms. The K entries match I + beta*N + t*J with N[i][j] = 1 iff j -/-> i. e_2 <= (B-Nn)(1+2t) held at every point.
